speaker: The Rescuer
before: A friend. That's all I can say, there isn't much time.
after: A friend. That's all I can say. There isn't much time.

speaker: The Rescuer
before: That will have to do. The path-ologists are hunting us.
after: That will have to do. The Path-ologists are hunting us.

speaker: The Rescuer
before: Behind me is the Forgotten Cave. Follow it all the way through to {town}. Someone there will be waiting for you.
after: Behind me is the Forgotten Cave. Follow it all the way through to {town}. Elder Maren will be waiting for you. Find her first.

speaker: The Rescuer
before: Hear that? They're close, but they do not know of this place, few do.
after: Hear that? They're close, but they don't know about this place. Few do.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: She's gone, and she's leading them away. By the way they're shouting I do not want to be caught by them.
after: She's gone, and she's leading them away. By the sound of their shouting, I do not want to be caught by them.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: No point getting lost twice in one day. Back to the cave.
after: No point getting lost twice in one day. Back up the path to the glowing arch.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: Whoever that was said help would be waiting on the other side. Whatever is inside the cave seems like a better option than those path-ologists.
after: Whoever that was said help would be waiting on the other side. Whatever is inside the cave seems like a better option than those Path-ologists.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: If you really don't remember anything you might be here awhile. You should get acquainted with the townsfolk. Say hello to Sable, Tilly and Pip on the square, and buy a card from Sable. Then come back.
after: If you really don't remember anything, you might be here awhile. You should get acquainted with the townsfolk. Say hello to Sable, Tilly and Pip on the square, and buy a card from Sable. Then come back.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Have you found answers to any of your questions? I can't deny, I am intrigued despite my better judgment .
after: Have you found answers to any of your questions? I can't deny, I am intrigued despite my better judgment.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Ten years ago {kingdom} was whole. Beefcakes made the energy, Gourmands fed us, Necrocrats minded the dead, Refusemancers hauled the waste and grew the crops.
after: Ten years ago {kingdom} was whole. Beefcakes made the energy, Gourmands fed us, Necrocrats minded the dead, Refusemancers hauled the waste and grew the crops. Everyone complained. Everything worked.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Still here, dearie? The roads won't walk themselves. Well. Some of them would, if {villain} let them.
after: Still here, dearie? {villain} would love you to sit by my fire forever. Don't give him the satisfaction. Give me back my chair.

speaker: Sable
before: You start with plain neutral cards. The Paths are where the power is. Browse, buy, then put it all to work at the Deck Station.
after: You start with plain neutral cards, darling: honest, dependable, dull. The Paths are where the power is. Buy some, then put them to work at the Deck Station.

speaker: Tilly Tonic
before: Potions and charms, back for more! Equip them on your Character screen for fights - maybe skip the orange one until I stop matching it!
after: Back for more potions! Equip them on your Character screen before a fight! Maybe skip the orange one until I stop matching it!

speaker: (narration)
before: Whatever it is, it is not open for business.
after: Whatever it is, it sounds like it has been on hold for a very long time.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: I will be here, guarding the drawer.
after: I will be here, guarding the drawer. The drawer does not know. That is the point.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: Whatever is down there is not open for business. Yet.
after: Somewhere below, very faintly, someone is rehearsing the word CHAMPION. Not yet, apparently.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: Whenever you collect more copies of a card than you can carry, the extras turn into essence of that card's Path.
after: When you collect more copies of a card than you can carry, dear, the extras boil down into essence of that card's Path. Nothing goes to waste here.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: And the Capital's mantle... well. Someone has to defeat the person who owns it first.
after: And the Capital's mantle... well. Someone must defeat its owner first. The mantle, frankly, is rooting for you.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: A champion who fights with every Path at once, and has a hand on every card. Bring your best deck.
after: A champion who fights with every Path at once, and has a fist for each. Bring your best deck.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: Another win for the books. The crowd roars (and tosses you some coins).
after: ANOTHER WIN FOR THE BOOKS! (normal voice) Some coins for you. From the crowd. The crowd is me.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: The puzzle got the better of you. Study the board and try again.
after: THE PUZZLE WINS THIS ROUND! (normal voice) Study the board. Try again. It's not going anywhere.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Walk into a town, and its station wakes up. Then you can rip between any two of them. Thank you for ripping with the Express.
after: After that, you can rip between any two stations. Thank you for ripping with the Express. Please keep your elbows inside the sky.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Spotter! Big news. You know that forest where you all started out?
after: Spotter! Big news. You know that forest outside town, where you first turned up?

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Fact: bears cannot open the drawer. Nobody opens the drawer. Protocol One.
after: Fact: bears cannot open the drawer. Nobody opens the drawer. Protocol Three.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: The flasks are humming today, dear. Don't touch the red one. It bites.
after: The flasks all bubbled when you passed, dear. Every colour. They never do that for me.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: Never lift alone. An old man told me that. Never broke, they say. Huh.
after: Never lift alone. An old man told me that. Haven't seen him in years. Huh.

speaker: Crosspath townsfolk
before: Lovely day for a quest, isn't it? Shh. Not too lovely. Somebody's listening.
after: Say what you like about His Perfection, the wells are clean. Shh. Don't, actually.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: The bridge is drawn up on the far side of the gorge. Somebody very large is standing by the crank.
after: The bridge is drawn up on the far side of the gorge. Somebody very large is standing by the crank, shouting about hydration.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: YOU WANT THE CRANK? EARN YOUR TURN - TEN REPS OF PAIN!
after: YOU WANT THE CRANK? TEN REPS! NO REST! I HAVE NOT SAT DOWN SINCE SPRING! IT IS GOING GREAT!

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: NOBODY CROSSES THE GORGE WITHOUT A SPOTTER. I AM THE SPOTTER. SPOT THIS.
after: SPOTTERS ONLY. I AM SPOTTERS. ...SPOTTER. I AM ONE SPOTTER.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: HA! The pump is still MINE!
after: HA! THE PUMP IS STILL MINE! GO HOME AND HYDRATE! THAT IS AN ORDER, NOT CONCERN!

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: "Passed out mid-rep. Happens to the best of us. Happened to me in the spring of... well. The tab's on you.
after: "Passed out mid-rep. Happens to the best of us. Happened to me in the spring of... the spring of... well. Towel's on your tab.

speaker: Throwers and rippers
before: Shredna rolls her shoulders. "Calf Cove. Nobody's been out there in months.
after: Shredna rolls her shoulders. "Calf Cove. Did the old yeti say hello? ...Don't tell me. I don't care. Did he, though?

speaker: Throwers and rippers
before: No tools, just lats. I open doors by taking a very personal interest in the wall."
after: I don't open doors. I take a very personal interest in a wall until it gives up."

speaker: (narration)
before: Pushed by hand, by Beefcakes, since forever.
after: Pushed by hand, by Beefcakes, since forever. (The D.N.A. once asked for exact start times. We said "morning-ish".)

speaker: (narration)
before: Run it to power the grid. No actual hamsters. Hamsters are on break.
after: Run it to power the grid. No actual hamsters. The hamsters get breaks.

speaker: (narration)
before: East to west. A courtesy chuck, the long way. Gym Rat card required for the long way.
after: East to west. A courtesy chuck, the long way. Gym Rat card required; Coach Benchley sells them.

speaker: (narration)
before: The regime's stronghold. Authorized personnel only.
after: The regime's stronghold. Authorized personnel only. Authorization takes thirty seconds, by order of the Minister of Efficiency.

speaker: (narration)
before: You see a regime enforcer flexing at nobody. Since breakfast, apparently; even his audience is exhausted.
after: You see a regime enforcer flexing at nobody. He has held the pose since breakfast, because nobody has told him he can stop.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Shh. Welcome to the Gainlands. The regime has ears. Big ones. I'm Old Man Mountain. We Beefcakes power the kingdom on mills and hamster wheels, and move folks by throw and by portal.
after: Shh. Welcome to the Gainlands. The regime has ears. Big ones. Old Man Mountain. We Beefcakes keep the kingdom's lights on and its folks moving. Wheels, mills... and if you're in a hurry, we throw you.

speaker: Professor Pump
before: Fifteen concern biceps; the regime burned the other two, so I rewrote them from memory. You cannot confiscate a well-trained brain-cep.
after: Fifteen concern biceps. The other two were a history of the Lifting Festival; the regime burned those, so I rewrote them from memory. You cannot confiscate a well-trained brain-cep.

speaker: Professor Pump
before: Answer well for gold and glory. Answer poorly and receive a mild, scholarly sigh. Today, we train the brain-ceps.
after: Answer well for gold and glory. Answer poorly and receive a mild, scholarly sigh. I have practised the sigh. It is devastating.

speaker: Professor Pump
before: Another lap! The Gainlands pay a small processing fee for repeat attendance.
after: Another lap! The Gainlands pay a little less for repeat attendance. The regime calls it a "processing fee". A D.N.A. phrase, I suspect.

speaker: Chet Thunderabs
before: Not quite a set, champ. That's fine. Take a breath.
after: Not quite a set, champ! But WAIT - that wasn't a failure! That was a FREE TRIAL!

speaker: Gym attendant
before: Gym's open! The weights are not. Regime orders. Enjoy the mirrors.
after: Gym's open! The weights are not. The scales stayed, though - standard measures, from the Capital. Say what you like, they never lie.

speaker: (narration)
before: You receive an empty cup. The stand has mistaken protein for a serving suggestion.
after: You receive an empty cup. Flavour: surprise.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: The Swole Station's lights are back on, and the grid's HUMMING. Take your reward before I turn this into a pep talk.
after: The Swole Station's lights are back on. Grid's humming. I'd make a speech, but all my energy went into the lights. Take your reward.

speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
before: Regime brutes, golems and sprites keep eating my deliveries! Beat any three roaming enemies in the Gainlands in card duels - END THE BULKING ORDERS!
after: Regime brutes, golems and sprites keep eating my deliveries! Beat any three roaming enemies in the Gainlands in card duels! THOSE SHAKES HAD MY NAME ON THEM!

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Just measuring. Lovely broad shoulders round here. Very roomy work. Heh.
after: Just measuring. Lovely broad shoulders round here. Very roomy work, when it comes. It hasn't, lately. Heh.

speaker: Baron Quadzilla, the Leg Press Lord
before: Baron Quadzilla racks the plates, stands, and wobbles. 'Huh,' he says. 'Standing. Wobbly. Like a first rep.'
after: Baron Quadzilla racks the plates, stands, and wobbles. 'Huh,' he says, looking down. 'So those are my feet. Hello, feet.'

speaker: (narration)
before: Rows of lockers hold the old champions' gear, every strap labelled by weight class. A laminated sign reads LOCKER 13 IS A STATE OF MIND. One door hangs ajar, humming the theme from a boxing movie.
after: Rows of lockers hold the old champions' gear, every strap labelled by weight class. A laminated sign reads LOCKER 13 IS A STATE OF MIND. One door hangs ajar, humming a training-montage tune to itself.

speaker: (narration)
before: Every weight the regime ever took. Behind a locker door, and behind a very sad sign.
after: Every weight the regime ever took, stacked behind one locker door. Each plate still has its owner's name chalked on the back.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex
before: The rounds are irregular. Listen for them on the stairs.
after: Their squats are not regular, so neither are the rounds. Listen for the knees on the stairs.

speaker: (narration)
before: You read the plate on the empty pedestal: GRANDMASTER FLEX (PENDING). The space above it remains empty.
after: You read the plate on the empty pedestal: GRANDMASTER FLEX (PENDING). It has been dusted. Recently.

speaker: (narration)
before: No spotter needed on the roof. He is holding that pose for himself.
after: Wave, and he will wave back. After the pose. The pose may take a while.

speaker: (narration)
before: (Town. Stairs sold separately. The cardio checkpoint has been repurposed as a snack bar.)
after: (To town. The cardio checkpoint is a snack bar now. Snacks are mandatory.)

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: YOU DID IT. Flex is out, Clench is down, and I got to watch. Best day since... since the last best day. I'll be spotting you for the rest of your HP, like it or not.
after: YOU DID IT. Flex is out, Clench is down, and I got to watch. Best day since... since the last best day. I'm spotting you from now on, like it or not.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
before: Clench is learning to lift from zero. The strongest take the longest. The gym is open to everyone now. Come whenever you like.
after: Clench is learning to lift from zero. The strongest take the longest. Yesterday he spotted Gary without being asked. The gym is open to everyone now; come whenever you like.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
before: The great pantry door swings open. Somewhere beyond, something smells incredible.
after: The great pantry door swings open. Somewhere beyond, something smells incredible. Underneath it, faintly, something smells of hot iron.

speaker: (narration)
before: Your HP is full, and the chef says there are no seconds. You both know this is a serving of fiction.
after: Your HP is already full. A chef refills your plate anyway. Here, being full is treated as a misunderstanding.

speaker: (narration)
before: A hidden stash! Nobody tasted that one. Lettuce rejoice.
after: A hidden stash! Unsampled, unsauced and all yours.

speaker: (narration)
before: You fell in the gravy! Somebody fishes you out and sets you on dry ground. (-1 HP)
after: You fall in the gravy. A passing chef fishes you out with a ladle and checks you for seasoning. (-1 HP)

speaker: (narration)
before: The golem steps aside. The way is open.
after: The golem steps aside with the slow dignity of a roast being carved. The way is open.

speaker: (narration)
before: You ladle some soup. Delicious, but you are already stuffed to the brim.
after: You ladle some soup, look at it, and pour it back. You are full. The fountain takes it well.

speaker: (narration)
before: - Guard the kingdom (with golems)
after: - Guard the kingdom (with golems. Defensive golems. Please stop saying the other word.)

speaker: (narration)
before: Welcome to the far side. The gates ahead are guarded by golems, as is the custom.
after: Welcome to the far side. The gates ahead are guarded by golems, as is the custom. One wants saffron, one wants a favour, one wants a fight.

speaker: (narration)
before: Please do not bite the buildings. They are load-bearing cake.
after: Please do not bite the buildings. The mayor's house is down to two layers, and he knows it was a visitor.

speaker: (narration)
before: Four ingredients, in the right order, tastes like victory.
after: Four ingredients, in the right order. Anything else tastes like a lesson.

speaker: Basil
before: Psst. Hello. I'm Basil, line cook. Ladle in one hand, nerves in the other. We Gourmands feed the kingdom and protect it. Every plate is a promise. Every golem is a guard.
after: Psst. Basil, line cook. Ladle in one hand, nerves in the other. We Gourmands feed the kingdom and protect it: chefs cook, golems guard. Lately the golems have been... practising.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: Don't tell the Grand Chef I said anything. She hears everything. She just never tastes anything.
after: Don't tell the Grand Chef I said anything. Last cook who complained got promoted to taste tester. We haven't seen him since.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: I'm hungry and a bit scared. If either came with a side dish, we'd be sorted.
after: I'm so hungry I looked at a Refusemancer compost heap and thought 'starter'. Don't tell anyone. I'd never live it down.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: Gourmand-issue, inspected by the Test Kitchen as of this year. The stamp is on the decorative cake, which has never looked more unappetizing.
after: Gourmand-issue, inspected by the Test Kitchen as of this year. They stamped my decorative cake. Right on the rosette. I have not forgiven them.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: The pantry's stocked until tomorrow, when we do it all again. Fetching has a wonderful sense of repetition; I'd like to send it back.
after: The pantry's stocked until tomorrow, when we do it all again. I'm not complaining. I'm fetching. They look similar from a distance.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: One Hearty Pot Pie, darling. Honey, basil and a ghost pepper into the Grand Oven by the arch. I shall wait. I have cake.
after: One Hearty Pot Pie, darling. Honey, basil and a ghost pepper into the Grand Oven by the arch. I shall wait. I have a cake to look at.

speaker: Professor Pate
before: Back to improve your score? Splendid. Knowledge, like a good roux, wants patience. And butter. Mostly butter.
after: Back for more? Splendid. A footnote, while it simmers: the Capital's school lunches were excellent once. Hot, free, balanced. Then came the paste.

speaker: (gate golem)
before: The golem stands firm.
after: The golem stands firm, like an aspic that has made up its mind.

speaker: Colonel Casserole
before: En garde, traveller. A duel of honour. Lids up. Yes, Chef.
after: En garde! Thirty years of service, and I have never once boiled over. Until now. Yes, Chef.

speaker: (narration)
before: You find rations, ladles and ladle-shaped weapons. Take what you can carry; someone has overthought serving suggestions.
after: You find rations, ladles and ladle-shaped weapons in crates marked SERVING UTENSILS (DEFENSIVE). Take what you can carry.

speaker: (narration)
before: Great vats of the Special Sauce bubble in the dark. This is where the corruption is made.
after: Great vats of the Special Sauce bubble in the dark. A clipboard on the rail reads: BATCH 3,652. TASTED BY: (blank).

speaker: (narration)
before: Blueprints, recipe cards and signed memos fill the cabinets. Every handwritten note signed by the Grand Chef leans the wrong way, as if written by someone who has only ever read about left-handedness.
after: Blueprints, recipe cards and signed memos fill the cabinets. Every note signed by the Grand Chef is in perfect copperplate, without one gravy stain. Real chefs' notes are mostly gravy stain.

speaker: (narration)
before: - Guard the kingdom (with golems)
after: - Guard the kingdom (with golems; the cannons are ovens now)

speaker: (narration)
before: To {town}, through the great pantry door. Wipe your feet - we just mopped, but your sample is yours now; take two.
after: To {town}, through the great pantry door. Wipe your feet; we just mopped. Free samples by the door. Take two. Nobody is checking.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: Tarragon! Sous-Chef! Free!
after: Tarragon! Sous-Chef! Fetcher of things! I caught up with lunch!

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: Official likeness withdrawn. It never captured the person who fed us.
after: Official likeness withdrawn. It never captured the person who fed us. (Also: whose chin is that?)

speaker: (narration)
before: You are already as rested as the dead get. Which is very rested. Technically, eternally.
after: You are already as rested as the dead get, and the dead get very rested.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
before: Parking Lot D has been renamed Parking Lot Dead. Please stop asking why.
after: Beefcake couriers: throwing a parcel through the window is not 'delivery'. Neither is throwing the courier.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: Per my last email: still serving 3. I don't have email. I hope the phrase conveys that I have asked before.
after: Per my last memo: still serving 3. Per the memo before that: also 3.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Back again? Loyalty is rewarded here. Not with money. With more work.
after: Back again, dear? Nobody else leaves. Since the transfer, not one soul has passed on. Not even me.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: The Records Basement elevator needs Form 13-B. I don't have one. Nobody does. It builds character.
after: The Records Basement elevator needs Form 13-B. I don't have one. Nobody does. I applied, but the application form is a 13-B.

speaker: Director Ectomund
before: Re-certified again. The Department pays a small processing fee for the paperwork.
after: Re-certified again. For the paperwork, the Department pays you a small processing fee. It has never paid in that direction before.

speaker: Director Ectomund
before: Try again. The signs aren't going anywhere. Neither, technically, is anyone here.
after: Try again. The signs aren't going anywhere. Since the transfer, neither is anyone here.

speaker: Director Ectomund
before: One correct. Your token. My interest remains non-refundable.
after: One correct. Your token. I have noted your potential in the margin, in very small writing.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: I took a number. Heh. It's a big one.
after: I took a number. Heh. Makes a change. Usually I'm the one calling them.

speaker: Kyle (Deceased Since '09)
before: brb, haunting. actually stay. nobody reads the 'be right back' part.
after: brb, haunting. been brb since '09. it's a long b.

speaker: Betty Bones, Surly Secretary
before: Take a number. The number is irrelevant. Take it anyway.
after: Take a number. I won't be calling it. Take it anyway.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Agnes Overdue. Front desk, and on my lunch hour, appellant. I stopped counting the appeals. Every one denied.
after: Agnes Overdue. Front desk, and on my lunch hour, appellant. Forty thousand appeals, every one denied. They've started decorating the stamps.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
before: Every important document in the Hall passes through here. It must be stamped, signed and witnessed by a notary.
after: Every important document in the Hall is stamped, signed and witnessed here. The transfer of authority was, too. The notary is still finding blue-green feathers.

speaker: Kyle
before: the queue moved. like, actually moved. my number's coming up in only four hundred years. new personal best.
after: the queue moved. like, actually moved. agnes called my number at 3am. i was afk. she called it again. nobody's ever called me twice.

speaker: Director Ectomund
before: Back again. The Department has reopened its records to honest examination, so I examine with a clear conscience now.
after: Back again. The ethics questions have been returned to the building. Not yet to the exam. One reform at a time.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Head of the whole Department, and still on the front desk. Old habits, dear. Ghosts were never good at being in one place.
after: Head of the whole Department, and still on the front desk. They gave me a big office, dear. Nobody waits in a big office. They wait here.

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
before: The Rot took Archdruid Compostella first, at the Rotheart, deep in the Verdant Dump. Everything else grew out from her.
after: The Rot took Archdruid Compostella first, at the Rotheart, deep in the Verdant Dump. Everything grew out from her. Me too, the day a very tidy lady with shears came calling.

speaker: (narration)
before: You eat roast roots and a pie with a crust like a fence post. The mug is mostly apple. You are thoroughly farm-fed. HP restored.
after: You eat roast roots and a pie with a crust like a fence post. The mug is mostly apple. A goat watches every bite. HP restored.

speaker: Dump workers
before: New stairs. Same climb. I was hoping they would fix that.
after: New stairs. Same climb. And the stairs grew two more steps overnight.

speaker: Dump workers
before: Every terrace a little higher, every terrace a little weirder. That's the Dump for you.
after: The Buffet calls us garbage eaters. Half our garbage is their souffle, barely touched.

speaker: (narration)
before: The belt has never lost a piece of sleep over your performance.
after: The belt does not slow down for anyone. It has been asked.

speaker: (narration)
before: A pile of tyres, doors and ambition across the gap.
after: A pile of tyres, doors and one very stubborn wardrobe across the gap.

speaker: (narration)
before: A trash golem towers over you, moss coating its fridge body. Something sprouts from its ears. This is no place for a cool head.
after: A trash golem towers over you, moss coating its fridge body. Something sprouts from its ears. Inside, the little light is still on.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: We are the Refusemancers: druids of waste removal and agriculture. Our animals eat the kingdom's garbage and turn it into fertilizer, and our magic helps the crops grow.
after: We are the Refusemancers: druids of waste removal and agriculture. Our animals turn the kingdom's garbage into fertilizer for its crops. The Buffet calls us garbage eaters. They eat our carrots.

speaker: Granny Gristle
before: Shop's open, dearie! Turnips are a day old. A lovely vintage, if you're a turnip.
after: Back again, dearie! Turnips are a day old. A lovely vintage, if you're a turnip.

speaker: Billie Muckfoot
before: The boar and goat in the stables will carry you. Ask nicely. Ask rudely. They don't speak either. Good, sensible animals.
after: The boar and goat in the stables will carry you. Ask nicely or ask rudely; they ignore both the same. Good, sensible animals.

speaker: His Majesty the Raccoon
before: 'WE DID NOT EAT THE COMPOST. We sampled it.' His Majesty grips the throne. 'The royal tasting is not open to questions.'
after: 'WE DID NOT EAT THE COMPOST. We... sampled it.' His Majesty grips the throne. 'The royal tasting is not open to questions.'

speaker: (narration)
before: Normal-looking plants, mostly. They are a little too green. Everything is alive in a way that feels like it is watching you.
after: Normal-looking plants, mostly. A little too green. Every leaf turns, very slightly, to follow you.

speaker: (narration)
before: The vines are choosing who gets through. Can your deck keep its footing?
after: The vines are choosing who gets through. They are reading your deck very closely.

speaker: Hortensia Clipwell, Royal Groundskeeper
before: Such a pretty weed. Such a shame. Now, stand still while I tidy you.
after: Gentlemen, if you would. He is well over regulation height.

speaker: (narration)
before: It tastes of rain and regret. You feel hardier, and a little poisoned.
after: It tastes of rain and old boots. You feel hardier, and a little poisoned.

speaker: (narration)
before: A tunnel full of drifting spores. Whether you can walk through it depends on how well your deck has been built.
after: A tunnel of drifting spores. A well-built deck walks straight through. A loose one starts to sprout.

speaker: (narration)
before: You see light pour through the splitting Rotheart.
after: Light pours through the splitting Rotheart.

speaker: (narration)
before: You watch wildflowers follow the light outward through the Dump.
after: Wildflowers follow the light outward, field by field, through the Dump.

speaker: Granny Gristle
before: Shop's open! Day-old turnips. None looking at anybody. Finally, produce that knows when to look away. Heh!
after: Day-old turnips, dearie, and not one of them looking at anybody. Finally, produce with manners. Heh!

speaker: Compostella, the Rotheart, and Archdruid Compostella
before: Archdruid Compostella. I am told what happened to the barn. I cannot remember doing it. I will help put it right.
after: Archdruid Compostella. I am told what happened to the barn. I cannot remember doing it. The barn, I gather, remembers me. I will help put it right.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: You have earned the truth. I have been keeping more from you than I should.
after: You have earned the truth, so here is the first piece of it: I am not only a tortoise who bakes.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I wasn't sure I could trust you before. I am now.
after: I wasn't sure of you before. I am sure now. Mostly.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I have been hiding here ever since.
after: I have been hiding here ever since, with my hands in pie dough, where nobody would ask what else they had made.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: One Path left under {villain}'s thumb. The whole town is holding its breath. It's murder on my knees.
after: One Path left under {villain}'s thumb. The whole town is holding its breath. I can hold mine for a week. They cannot.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: The roads are open. Even the tortoises use them. I passed one this morning. Barely.
after: The roads are open. Even I use them. I passed a hare this morning. He has asked for a recount.

speaker: (narration)
before: You find a boot in the spring. Clear water slips around its heel. Even here, something finds a way through.
after: Someone has thrown a boot in the spring. The water has gone politely round it.

speaker: (narration)
before: You recall the first words of every Gourmand recipe: first, water. Someone has added 'and salt' here. Twice.
after: Every Gourmand recipe still begins with the same two words: first, water. Somebody has added 'and salt' here. Twice.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: A well with opinions. I'll take a bottle's worth.
after: A well with opinions. Fine. I'm keeping the bottle.

speaker: (narration)
before: The service-tunnel network is down. Nobody has run the wheels that power the shaft lifts in ten years. 'No travel,' says a Wrinkle's note on the hatch.
after: The service-tunnel network is down. The wheels that once turned the shaft lifts have spent ten years lighting the facade instead. 'No travel,' says a Wrinkle's note on the hatch.

speaker: (narration)
before: A real recipe, written by hand, with a stain of actual sauce on the corner! A pinch of this, a spoonful of that. It is wonderfully imprecise. You tuck it away.
after: A real recipe, written by hand, with a stain of actual sauce on the corner! Flour: some. Salt: enough. Time: until it smells right. It is wonderfully imprecise. You tuck it away.

speaker: (narration)
before: The second wheel has been turning since before some of its runners were old enough to vote. A foreman's whistle hangs from a hook. You take it off its hook and put it in your pocket.
after: The second wheel has been turning since some of its runners were too small to reach the pedals. A foreman's whistle hangs from a hook. You pocket it.

speaker: (narration)
before: The third wheel's crew are children. Children! 'It is a school activity,' says a banner.
after: The third wheel's crew are children in school caps. 'It is a school activity,' says a banner. Nobody has rung the bell.

speaker: (narration)
before: You watch the neighbourhood carry Mr. Pell to his grave. A quiet tune accompanies the coffin as they lower it.
after: You watch the neighbourhood carry Mr. Pell to his grave. Nobody holds a permit to sing, so they sing very quietly. Nobody stops them.

speaker: (narration)
before: The Beefcakes kept the kingdom's energy and its roads: the wheels, the mills, the throwers and the portal-rippers. {villain} put them all on wheels to light one small town. The rest of the kingdom went dark.
after: The Beefcakes kept the kingdom's energy and its roads: the wheels, the mills, the throwers and the portal-rippers. {villain} put them all on wheels to light one showpiece street. The rest of the kingdom went dark.

speaker: (narration)
before: A Showcase Quarter, built to show what the whole kingdom could be if everybody simply tried harder.
after: Every house in this quarter was built to show what the whole kingdom could be if everybody simply tried harder.

speaker: (narration)
before: To the Crease. The dead are not allowed down. The living are a little afraid of the dead down there. Be kind.
after: To the Crease. Living passengers only. The dead have asked to come down too; we are thinking about it. Be kind.

speaker: (narration)
before: The Paths tear where {villain} forced them into one shape. His hold is failing; the tears began the night someone escaped the Ministry.
after: The tears are temporary and fully under control. (Scrawled below: the Paths tear where {villain} forced them into one shape. His hold slipped the night someone escaped the Ministry.)

speaker: Wren
before: Back in one piece? Good. Mostly one piece.
after: Back in one piece? Good. Hesper charges by the piece.

speaker: Wren
before: The records say he began as a good man. Keep that in mind. It does not excuse what he has done.
after: The records say he began well. His first decree put a hot lunch in front of every schoolchild. Remember that. It excuses nothing.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: I talk to him in the parlour. I don't know what else to do. Please, if you can help.
after: I talk to him in the parlour. He was always the patient one. I'm not, it turns out. Please, if you can help.

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: I have measured eleven thousand visitors. I approved four. Nine thousand were sent home. The rest, I will not say.
after: I have measured twelve thousand visitors. I approved four. Nine thousand were sent home. The rest, I will not say.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Still above regulation. Still letting it go. Do not make me regret it.
after: Still one hair above regulation. I have thought about that hair all week. Do not make me regret it.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: Here. From the old days: what we gave people who could keep going.
after: Here... from the old days. We gave these out... at the end of a shift. Remember ends?

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: Everyone is so friendly! Everyone is so friendly. It is like living inside a greeting card.
after: Everyone is so friendly! Everyone is so friendly. It is like living inside a greeting card. The kind with nothing written in it.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Please continue to be happy, as scheduled! This has been your Deputy Minister of Good News!
after: Please continue to be happy, as scheduled! Lost Ministry property must be returned at once, and not spoken to!

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Attention, citizens! Please remember: the exits are for ENTERING. The entrances are for EXITING.
after: Great news, citizens! The public records have never been tidier! Every untidy page has been corrected!

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Anything else is an unapproved Direction.
after: If you remember things differently, please report to the Correction Ward. Your memory will be tidied too!

speaker: Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency
before: You. Again. You cost me the Gainlands in four hours and eleven minutes. I have had the figure framed.
after: You. Again. You cost me the Gainlands in four hours and twelve minutes. I have had the figure framed.

speaker: Old Fern
before: Granny Gristle needs hands on the compost rows down in the Dump. Peel from shell. Messy work.
after: Granny Gristle needs hands on the compost rows down in the Dump. Sorting peel from shell, all day. Messy. You'll hate it. Good.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: Trained with... the Gainlands wheel crews. They told us... it was cardio.
after: Back in the Gainlands... we threw commuters. Now I'd pay... to be thrown.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: The junction crew trains on scrap: tyre flips, bin presses, dumbbells made of drain pipe. Every Garbage becomes muscle.
after: Beefcake bore, Gourmand vents, Necrocrat signs, Refusemancer drains. The junction crew lifts the scrap. Every Garbage becomes muscle.

speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
before: HALT! This is a restricted pantry! Those recipes are confiscated for the war effort!
after: ATTENTION! This is a restricted pantry! Those recipes are confiscated for the war effort!

speaker: (narration)
before: 'Welcome,' says a quiet voice. 'Please wipe your feet. You are expected.'
after: 'Welcome,' says a quiet, polite voice from nowhere. 'Please wipe your feet. Please wipe your opinions. You are expected.'

speaker: (narration)
before: 'All Gourmands to be fed the sauce. They will be happier. They will no longer need to choose for themselves.'
after: All Gourmands to be fed the sauce. They will be happier, and a little less themselves. I consider this the improvement.'

speaker: (narration)
before: 'When the champion is weak, he will no longer be a disagreement. NOTE: he continues to train without the weights. Observe carefully.'
after: When the champion is sufficiently weak, he will no longer be a disagreement. NOTE: do not underestimate him. He does a lot of stretching.'

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Great news, citizens! The traitor has been located!
after: Great news, citizens! The traitor has been located! Please hold your applause until she has been removed.

speaker: (narration)
before: You see a curator patrol the side gallery, feather duster in hand. He straightens each frame without looking at its face. (A battle.)
after: A curator with a feather duster patrols the side gallery. Anything crooked, he straightens. Anything alive, he dusts. (A battle.)

speaker: (narration)
before: You face a clerk at a tall desk. His stamp falls rapidly; his eyes stay on the paper. (A battle.)
after: A clerk at a tall desk, stamping everything that moves. Quite fast. Quite sad. His eyes never leave the paper. (A battle.)

speaker: (narration)
before: You face a vast staircase. Every step is the same height; you cannot see the landing from the bottom. A story event.
after: A staircase so grand it has its own staircase. Every step is exactly the same height; you cannot see the landing from the bottom. A story event.

speaker: (narration)
before: You leave the cracked dome behind and return to the hall.
after: You leave the seed where it fell. Out of its dome it looks smaller. Most things here do. You go back.

speaker: (narration)
before: You sit in the reading chair. One person has worn a hollow in its seat. Beside you, lamplight shines through a handmade shade.
after: You sit in the old reading chair. It is worn exactly where one person sat, every night, for years. Someone made the lampshade by hand. It is a little crooked.

speaker: (narration)
before: You follow the lines of the plans with one finger. Then you roll up the best and take it. Your throat tightens.
after: They are good. They are so good. You roll up the best and take it, with something in your throat.

speaker: (narration)
before: You remove the old gold frame. The mirror remains hanging; you can still see yourself. The gold will sell for a good price.
after: You prise off the old gold frame and leave the mirror hanging, bare. It still shows whoever stands in front of it. It never needed the gold.

speaker: (narration)
before: You find the brass collection plate bolted to the wall, marked for {villain_title}. You take the coins.
after: A little brass plate for donations to {villain_title}, bolted to the wall. It is quite full. You take the lot.

speaker: (narration)
before: You close your hand around the money and leave the empty plate.
after: It is, after all, other people's money. They would want it back.

speaker: (narration)
before: You find a pot of coins on the top landing, left as a tip by the last climber. You rub your legs and pocket it.
after: At the top, a pot of coins sits on the landing: a tip left by the last person who made it. You rub your legs and pocket the coins.

speaker: (narration)
before: You keep reading. Page after page describes work that helped people.
after: It goes on. They are good. They are so good.

speaker: (narration)
before: You read the last plan twice. You recognise the care in it. You close the journal gently.
after: Once, he was exactly the person you would want running a kingdom. You close the last journal very gently.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: I've walked a long way. Everyone I met was afraid of you.
after: Sorry. That's forest mud. I've walked a long way, and everyone I met on the way here was afraid of you.

speaker: Primm
before: Every one of them has a number. I can account for every citizen. Nobody need be overlooked.
after: Every one of them has a number. Nobody is ever overlooked. Do you know how few kingdoms can say that?

speaker: Primm
before: Please remain still. I know how to put this right.
after: This will not hurt. It will, however, be Standard.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: People are different. You know that.
after: Because some things are five. Some people are.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: People are different. You know that.
after: Because some things are five. Some people are.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: I'm not your subject. No order outranks treating people with respect.
after: And nobody files me under 'subject' again. No order outranks treating people with respect.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: I'm not your subject. No order outranks treating people with respect.
after: Nobody files me under 'subject' again. No order outranks treating people with respect.

speaker: (battle UI)
before: Every unit, yours and his, is a 3/3. You may play at most two non-infrastructure cards a turn. (Two is the perfect number.)
after: Every unit, yours and his, starts as a 3/3; buffs and debuffs still change it. You may play at most two non-infrastructure cards a turn. (Two is the perfect number.)

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
before: You see Grandmaster Flex step from behind a pillar, unwinding a bandage from his arm. 'Breathe in. Hold.'
after: Grandmaster Flex steps out from behind a pillar, unwinding a very small bandage from a very large arm. 'Breathe in. Hold.'

speaker: The Grand Chef
before: You see the Grand Chef in a clean apron, ladle in hand. 'Have you eaten? Let me help.'
after: The Grand Chef, in a clean apron, ladle in hand. 'Have you eaten? No. Of course you have not.'

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: 'The rules must answer for him too.' (Agnes's Appeal: Necrocrat cards cost 1 less, and you gain 2 max HP.)
after: 'It applies to him, dear. It applies to him very well.' (Agnes's Appeal: Necrocrat cards cost 1 less, and you gain 2 max HP.)

speaker: (narration)
before: You stand among the pieces of the model. Tiny houses lie scattered across the floor. The table no longer holds a kingdom.
after: The model lies in pieces. A hundred thousand tiny houses on the floor, all in the wrong places, and somehow they look better.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: You took my mother and father. I can't even remember their faces. I'm letting go. I won't keep living in what you did.
after: You took my mother and father. I can't even remember their faces. I'm letting it go anyway. Watch.

speaker: (narration)
before: You hear the mirrors crack one by one. For the first time in ten years, {villain} sees himself in them.
after: The mirrors crack one by one, and for the first time in ten years {villain} sees himself in them.

speaker: (narration)
before: Above the small kingdom, you see a tired man kneeling without his crown or his perfect smile.
after: No crown. No perfect smile. Only a tired man kneeling above a very small kingdom.

speaker: (narration)
before: You stand in the light pouring through the broken glass.
after: Light pours in through the broken glass. It does not feel like winning. It feels like the end of a long, quiet lie.

speaker: (narration)
before: The Necrocrat wing's archive is filing from floor to ceiling. On the desk, under a paperweight shaped like a peacock, lies a memo, the ink still wet.
after: The Necrocrat wing's archive is paper from floor to ceiling. On the desk, under a paperweight shaped like a peacock, lies a memo, the ink still wet.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
before: 'Fell over. We rolled you in. Fee is yours. Drink the tea while it is hot; freedom hasn't changed that part.'
after: 'Fell over. We rolled you in. The fee is still yours. The tea is not free just because the kingdom is.'

speaker: Old Fern
before: Smell that? Honest compost. I could cry. Waste of water when I could be watering the patch. Come back any time.
after: Smell that? Honest compost. I could cry. Won't. Waste of good water. Come back any time.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: We visit every morning. I tell him about the people who helped us. I tell him about you.
after: We're well. My husband would have said you were late. He'd have meant it fondly.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: Flour on the ceiling. Food on the plates. Everything in its proper place, at last.
after: And chaotic. There is flour on the ceiling. I have never been so happy to have a mess.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: A hat of any size. I keep looking up, trying to decide.
after: I am going to wear a hat of any size. Maybe two at once.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: The bakery is painted on. We want a real one. None of us knows how to bake yet. Anyone can volunteer to be the first to burn a loaf.
after: The bakery is painted on. There is going to be a real one, as soon as someone learns to bake. I have a recipe. The recipe is: try.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: The hedge is round. I kept trimming the corners, and then I wondered why I wanted corners.
after: The hedge is round. The hedge wanted to be round. I asked it. I did not have to submit a form.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: Spontaneity every day! I don't know what comes next! I can hardly wait!
after: Spontaneity every day! I am exhausted! I am not sure I like it! I love it!

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: May I be honest? Your hat is awful. Thank you for wearing it.
after: I am not going to be polite today. I am going to be honest. Your hat is awful. I love it.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Attention, citizens! Any hat size is permitted. You may finally stop thinking about hat sizes.
after: Attention, citizens! Hats of any size are now permitted. Hats of negative size remain under review.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Attention, citizens! Spontaneity is no longer limited to Thursday. You may disregard this reminder.
after: Attention, citizens! Spontaneity Thursday is now every day. You may stop rehearsing your surprise.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Attention, citizens. The Wrinkles were real. Please thank them.
after: Attention, citizens. The Wrinkles were real. Please thank anyone who exists.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Nobody has told me where else to stand. I keep almost asking permission to go for a walk.
after: Nobody has told me where else to stand. I thought I might go for a walk. If that is... No. I am not asking. I am telling you. I think.

speaker: (narration)
before: You hear the scale model split. The table cracks beneath it, and the sound travels through the castle walls.
after: The scale model cracks in half. Then the table cracks. Then, with the sound of a very large drawer being pulled from a very large cabinet, the castle walls begin to come down.

speaker: (narration)
before: In {showcase}, a painted door falls flat. You see a citizen step through onto the street beyond.
after: In {showcase}, a painted door falls flat, and a very surprised citizen steps through it onto a very real street.

speaker: (narration)
before: You see Fig Sly among the people emerging from the Crease. He carries his stock with him.
after: Fig Sly comes up out of the Crease already selling something, to somebody, for some reason. Nobody stops him.

speaker: (narration)
before: You watch the four Paths gather around their leaders, carrying what they have saved from the past ten years.
after: The Beefcakes are late. The Necrocrats have brought a form. The Gourmands are overdressed. The Refusemancers smell, faintly, of compost.

speaker: (narration)
before: You see hands marked by iron, flour, ink and soil reach across the space between the four groups.
after: Muscle and stoves, records and soil: each was good alone. Together they ran a kingdom, argued about it every day, and it worked.

speaker: (narration)
before: You read the changes beneath it: MAY crossed out for SHOULD, then WILL, IF THEY FEEL LIKE IT. Four hands have left their marks.
after: Somebody has crossed out MAY and written SHOULD. Somebody else has crossed out SHOULD and written WILL, IF THEY FEEL LIKE IT. A pigeon sits on the full stop.

speaker: (narration)
before: For everyone who waited to be heard.
after: In memory of Form 27-B, Form 27-C and Form 27-B

speaker: (narration)
before: For everyone learning to choose again.
after: No hats were harmed. Several were enlarged.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Thank you, dear. I have written it down, though that hardly seems enough.
after: I have filed a Form of Gratitude, dear. It was approved on the first attempt. Irregular.

speaker: (narration)
before: the Pathwork Throne
after: The Pathwork Throne

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: You see Maren make her way through the crowd. She stops in front of you, flour still on her sleeve.
after: Maren pushes through the crowd, tortoise-slow, and stops in front of you. There is flour on her sleeve.

speaker: Primm, "His Perfection"
before: He designs good drains. The guard stays here while he works.
after: He designs very good drains, it turns out. Do not tell him I said so.

speaker: Isla Brannoch
before: You're the one who knocked the castle over? Dad says hi. Dad says a lot, actually. Thank you.
after: You're the one who knocked the castle over? Dad says thank you. That's what the 'Hm' meant. Thank you from me, too.

speaker: (narration)
before: In the Capital's square, you watch the leaders of the four Paths clasp hands. Several people cry.
after: In the Capital's square, the leaders of the four Paths clasp hands. Nobody trips. Several people cry.

speaker: (narration)
before: Above you, four banners share one crowded pole.
after: Four banners fly from the same pole. It is a little crowded, and nobody minds.

speaker: (narration)
before: At the crowd's edge, you see a hooded traveler smile, leaves still in their hair. There is always another path.
after: At the edge of the crowd, a hooded traveler smiles, leaves still in their hair. There is always another path.

speaker: (narration)
before: A round chamber, glass on every side, a chair at the center with straps worn pale. Cables run from the chair to four great tanks, each glowing a different color. This is where it was done.
after: A round chamber, glass on every side, a chair at the center with straps worn pale. Cables run from the chair to four great tanks, each glowing a different colour. This is where it was done.

speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
before: Get up, Dad. You're going to Crosspath. Agnes has a form for you, Maren has a great deal to say, and you are going to listen to all of it.
after: Get up, Dad. You're going to {town}. Agnes has a form for you, Maren has a great deal to say, and you are going to listen to all of it.

speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
before: No. It was yours too. Get up. You're going to Crosspath, and you're going to listen to every word Maren says.
after: No. It was yours too. Get up. You're going to {town}, and you're going to listen to every word Maren says.
